title: Stop Guessing with OAuth: Understanding CI/CD
summary: OAuth 2.0 is the leading open authorization framework that enables secure delegated access to protected resources.
body_text: OAuth 2.0 is the leading open authorization framework that enables secure delegated access to protected resources. From traditional web apps and browser-based apps to native apps and desktop applications, OAuth allows client apps to grant access on a user’s behalf without exposing login credentials, enabling powerful third-party applications, custom data flows, and powerful user experiences. However, while OAuth is secure, it’s not always fast. Guesswork and synthetic tests often fail to reveal latency issues in authorization code exchanges, token requests, and refresh token workflows, which can lead to problems for providers, including slow authentication, expired sessions, and poor user experiences. Speedscale brings realism to performance testing of OAuth by capturing live traffic between the client app, authorization server, and resource server. It records OAuth flows, including the authorization code flow, client credentials, and implicit flow, and allows providers to replay them under pressure to benchmark the whole lifecycle. Automation of the build and test process with Speedscale ensures that OAuth flows are built and validated efficiently, reducing manual effort, increasing reliability, and helping to catch bugs early in the development cycle. Using Speedscale, you can test from start to finish, from the authorization endpoint to token issuance and resource access, ensuring your system works the way you want it to and with the right overhead. Today, we’re going to dive into OAuth validation and look at how Speedscale can optimize access token exchange, client secret verification, and refresh token issuance before users ever even encounter issues in production. Automation in CI/CD pipelines helps prevent bugs, increases reliability, and boosts developer productivity by ensuring that each build is thoroughly tested and built for performance. Understanding OAuth 2.0 Flows, Grant Types, and Common Latency Sources While OAuth is a powerful solution for authorisation, it can introduce some latency issues when improperly configured or tested. To understand why this is, let’s examine the critical steps in a standard OAuth process. OAuth 2.0 is often mistaken for an authentication protocol, but it is primarily an authorization protocol designed to grant access to resources rather than verify user identities. There are several grant types in OAuth 2.0, each applicable to different use cases and security requirements. Authorization Request Here, the client app constructs an authorization request to the authorization endpoint, including the client ID, redirect URL, and requested scopes. This request kicks off the authorization protocol that is broadly referred to as a “flow”, and while this flow can differ depending on what you’re trying to do, the following steps are generally the same. Authorization Server Authenticates At this stage, users authenticate at the authorization server, entering login credentials or passing multi-factor authentication, thereby granting delegated access to their user data. It’s important to remember that this is delegated access, which differs from federated access or other identity layer controls. In essence, the user is giving a system permission to use their credentials to do work on their behalf. Authorization Code Grant In the authorization code flow, the authorization server returns an authorization code to the redirect URI. The client app exchanges the code, along with the client secret, for an access token. This access token informs the system that the entity holding it is authorized to act on the user’s behalf, serving as a security badge or delegation credential. Access Token Usage Next, the access token, typically a JSON Web Token (JWT), is sent in HTTP requests to the resource server to access resources and validate this access against validation rulesets. This token contains everything necessary to validate that the delegated access is intended, is current, is valid, and is for the resources being accessed. Refresh Token Flow Notably, when this access token expires, the client app sends a token request including the refresh token to obtain a new access token without forcing the end user to reauthenticate. This allows tokens to be revoked and ensures that captured OAuth tokens can’t be used to bypass limited access or authorize access in the future outside of the current request. The Core Concern - Latency While this flow changes depending on what kind of request is made and which grant types are involved, the steps are generally the same. Keen eyes might notice, however, that this multistep process, although it’s efficient, is nonetheless still a multistep process. The reality is that each step can introduce latency: cryptographic signing of tokens, database lookups for client credentials, network round-trips, and JSON signature validation. Under load, these latencies can compound, impacting user experiences in web applications and API-driven services. While most OAuth instances aren’t going to suffer overtly from authorization flows and the core OAuth protocol, these issues can certainly compound. When latency hits a roadblock, it can climb quite quickly. Accordingly, the name of the game is testing, and testing often. If you can ensure your flows work right in pre-production, you can make sure your system will work under real load. OAuth Security: Protecting Your Tokens and Flows Securing your OAuth implementation is just as important as optimizing its performance. The authorization protocol is designed to safeguard access to sensitive data, but without the right security practices, even the most robust OAuth flows can be vulnerable to threats. As a developer, it’s your responsibility to ensure that every aspect of your OAuth deployment—from traffic capture to token issuance—is protected against unauthorized access. A key part of this security is the use of secure protocols and tools throughout your workflow. When capturing and replaying traffic for testing, always use a trusted traffic replay tool that supports encrypted communication and enforces strict access controls. This ensures that captured traffic, including access tokens and authentication data, remains confidential and cannot be intercepted or misused during testing or analysis. The authorization server sits at the heart of your OAuth security posture. It must be configured to validate client credentials, enforce scope restrictions, and issue tokens only to authenticated and authorized clients. Regularly audit your authorization server’s configuration and monitor for unusual traffic patterns that could indicate abuse or attempted breaches. Integrating OAuth security checks into your continuous integration and continuous deployment pipelines is another best practice. Automated tests should verify that token endpoints are protected, that only valid clients can request tokens, and that expired or revoked tokens are handled correctly. By embedding these checks into your CI/CD process, you can catch security regressions before they reach production, maintaining a secure authorization protocol across every deployment. Finally, developers should stay up to date with evolving security standards and regularly review their OAuth implementation for potential vulnerabilities. Leverage tools that support secure traffic capture and replay, and follow industry best practices for token storage, transmission, and validation. By prioritizing security at every stage—from development to deployment—you can ensure that your OAuth flows remain resilient, your tokens stay protected, and your users’ data is always secure. Why Synthetic Tests Miss Critical Bottlenecks? It might be tempting to just throw as much synthetic data at the problem as possible and validate that your OAuth flows work. Unfortunately, synthetic testing is often quite problematic. Simple synthetic tests generate uniform HTTP requests, but they lack the dynamics of real OAuth clients and grant types: They don’t mimic browser-based apps following redirects to the authorization endpoint or desktop applications using implicit flow. They often ignore JSON Web Token (JWT) validation and token introspection calls that resource servers make. They fail to simulate client credentials grants for server-side machine-to-machine authentication protocols. Synthetic tests frequently fail to cover all possible test cases, missing critical scenarios that can occur in real-world environments. Additionally, synthetic tests lack the advanced features of modern traffic replay tools, such as the ability to handle complex OAuth flows and integration with CI/CD pipelines or Kubernetes. Without capturing actual grant types and token exchanges, teams can remain blind to performance pitfalls in the OAuth process. This is a scenario where the quality of your data can undermine your testing. The worse your testing data is, the worse your experience is going to be in production. The worse your user experience will be in practice. The best way to resolve this issue, then, is to skip synthetic data entirely. For example, a synthetic test might validate a simple token exchange but miss a real-world issue where a specific grant type fails due to a misconfigured redirect URI—something a traffic replay tool would catch. Capturing Real OAuth Traffic with Speedscale The answer is simple: use Speedscale! Speedscale enables you to capture the actual interactions between resource owner systems and client requests, modeling application access flows and the reality of third-party apps within your system to obtain a snapshot of the authorization state. Speedscale can capture traffic under real world conditions, reflecting the complexity of modern software applications and modern infrastructure such as Kubernetes and containerized environments. This allows you to test against authentic production scenarios, even as your infrastructure evolves. From here, you can insert your flow controls and test how they respond to increased, decreased, or even malicious traffic. Speedscale’s lightweight agents record traffic between OAuth clients, the authorization server, and resource servers: Capture Access Token Exchanges : Record the token request payloads, including grant types, client ID, client secret, and responses that contain access tokens, refresh tokens, and expiration dates. Sanitize Sensitive Data : Mask user authentication data, client secret values, and refresh tokens while preserving request structure and timing. Track Protected Resources : Capture calls to resource servers with access tokens accessing user data and bank account details in Read scopes. Manage Test Configurations : Easily manage and adjust test configurations to ensure accurate and repeatable results across different environments. This capture of real-world traffic ensures your tests include valid token lifecycles, scopes negotiation, and error scenarios like invalid grants or expired tokens. Speedscale uses advanced methods to capture and analyze traffic, ensuring comprehensive coverage of OAuth flows for even the most complex software applications and infrastructure. Again, this is a question of input quality - the better your data during testing, the more accurate your codebase will be, and the lower latency your authorization flows will generate. Replaying OAuth Workflows Under Load With captured OAuth flows, you can replay your traffic into staging environments, unlocking some pretty incredible benefits: Scale-Up Testing : Ramp parallel token requests to simulate thousands of OAuth clients performing authorization code flows or client credentials grants. Time-Accurate Replay : Preserve real inter-request intervals to emulate peak load bursts and token refresh storms. Error Injection : Introduce network delays or simulate authorization server downtime to test client retry and backoff logic. Replay testing can be integrated as an extension of your CI/CD pipeline, enabling automated integration tests after frequent merging of code changes. This approach reduces manual effort by triggering replay tests automatically, ensuring that different components work together before you deploy to production. By streamlining the deployment process, you can catch issues early and maintain a reliable, production-ready application. By using replay tests against your OAuth flow, you can reveal performance metrics for the entire OAuth lifecycle: authorization server issues time, resource server response, token introspection latency, and end-to-end round-trip times. Benchmarking and Optimizing Key OAuth Operations This whole process can help you not only identify potential issues in your current flow, it can also help you more efficiently optimize code structures to improve overall flow times. In many cases, you might not have a full “blocker” or critical error, but this testing process will still surface these imperfections, leading to a better system overall. Optimizing OAuth flows also helps address network configuration challenges, such as handling IP address restrictions or domain name resolutions, which ultimately improves the experience for your customers by ensuring smoother authentication and access. For instance, by tracking actual performance with Speedscale-captured data, you can test: Authorization Code Flow : Measure time from authorization request to new access token issuance. Optimize the authorization server’s code exchange endpoint and database pool settings. Client Credentials : Benchmark access token grants for microservices calling your APIs as OAuth clients. Right-size your authorization server for machine-to-machine traffic. Refresh Token Flow : Simulate large cohorts of expired tokens and measure refresh token request performance. Tune refresh token rotation policies. Resource Access : Test resource server handling of access tokens, JSON Web Token validation, and authorization checks under high concurrency. Selecting the right solutions for benchmarking and optimization is key to maintaining high performance and customer satisfaction. Speedscale can help unlock the ability to track performance percentiles - e.g., p50, p95, p99 - to pinpoint slow paths and guide tuning of the authorization server, caching userinfo responses, or optimizing JWK key rotations. This can not only help in your OAuth process, but in establishing, maintaining, and proving your client Service Level Agreements. Integrating OAuth Performance Testing into CI/CD With effective capture and replay in place, you can also start to integrate your performance testing processes into your general CI/CD pipelines. Speedscale is meant to be incorporated into these pipelines from day one, unlocking: Pre-Merge Gatekeeping : Run replay tests on pull requests to prevent performance regressions in token endpoints and resource access. Automated Benchmarks : Schedule nightly or weekly OAuth load tests covering all grant types: authorization code flow, implicit flow, client credentials, and refresh token flows. Observability Correlation : Tag replay sessions to connect Speedscale metrics with traces in OpenTelemetry or logs in centralized dashboards. Embedding realistic OAuth benchmarks into continuous integration and continuous deployment ensures secure authorization remains fast at every release, matching your expected service level while reducing overall latency due to authorization. Best Practices for OAuth Performance With all of this said, there are also some core OAuth performance best practices you should be building into your flow: Horizontal Scaling : Scale authorization servers and token services behind load balancers. You can use Speedscale’s record-and-replay data to size instance counts, getting closer to more accurate and responsive load balancing as well as more effective use of general resources. JWT Optimization : Use JSON Web Tokens with efficient signature algorithms to reduce introspection overhead on resource servers. The size of your JWT can have its latency concerns, so capturing real JWTs in practice can help you get a sense of whether or not your processing is as efficient as you want it to be. Adaptive Token Lifetimes : Balance short-lived tokens for security with longer TTLs to reduce frequent refreshes under heavy loads. Striking the right balance will again require some capture to see the balance in practice with real traffic. Edge Caching : Cache JWK sets and userinfo responses at API gateways or CDNs to speed up token verification. Optimizations guided by real OAuth traffic yield better results than guesses based on synthetic scripts, and Speedscale can give you that real traffic in spades. Conclusion OAuth is the cornerstone of modern authentication and authorization, but performance issues in the OAuth framework can lead to sluggish user experiences and frustrated developers when improperly configured or optimized. title: Why KYC is required to use global accounts (and how to do it easily)
summary: Here’s why you’re required to complete a KYC verification to use global accounts and how to do it easily.
body_text: Global accounts simplify cross-border payments by allowing users to easily access foreign bank accounts. Unlike traditional banks, Know Your Customer (KYC) verification acts like a network of vigilant security cameras and checkpoints, ensuring that only genuine users gain access to the payment platform. Without these checks, criminals could infiltrate the system, using it to launder money, fund illicit activities, or commit fraud, thereby endangering the entire financial system. KYC prevents such financial crimes by verifying the identity of every user, keeping global accounts safe and compliant. Whether you’re a freelancer receiving international payments, an entrepreneur expanding into new markets, or an individual managing multi-currency finances, KYC is the gatekeeper that protects the system. What is KYC? Know Your Customer (KYC) is a mandatory process used by financial institutions, fintech platforms, and other regulated entities to verify the identity of their customers. The process typically involves collecting and validating personal information, such as government-issued identification, proof of address, and, in some cases, additional documents like bank statements or tax identification numbers. KYC is an essential part of global financial regulations, designed to ensure transparency, security, and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorism financing (CTF) laws. For global accounts, KYC is particularly critical because they facilitate cross-border transactions. Also read: The best international bank accounts for freelancers and remote workers Why KYC is required for global accounts KYC validation helps fintechs maintain a secure, transparent, and compliant financial system. Below are the key reasons why KYC is relevant: 1. Prevents financial crime Global accounts facilitate transactions across countries, which can attract bad guys trying to exploit the system for illicit activities like money laundering, fraud, or terrorism financing. KYC ensures that financial institutions and fintech platforms know exactly who is using their services, reducing the risk of accounts being used for illegal purposes. By verifying identities, institutions can track money flow and flag suspicious activities, aligning with global AML and CTF regulations. 2. Regulatory compliance Financial institutions and fintech platforms operating globally must adhere to strict regulations set by bodies such as the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), the European Union’s Anti-Money Laundering Directives, or country-specific regulators like the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) in the UK. These regulations mandate KYC to ensure that businesses operate within legal frameworks, avoid penalties, and maintain their licences to operate. 3. Builds trust and security KYC fosters trust between users and service providers. When customers know that a platform verifies the identities of all its users, they feel more confident that their funds are secure (especially if their hands are clean). It also protects users from identity theft and fraud by ensuring that only authorised individuals can access and operate accounts. 4. Enables cross-border transactions Global accounts often involve multiple jurisdictions, each with its own regulatory requirements. KYC ensures that users meet the compliance standards of all relevant countries, enabling seamless cross-border transactions. Without KYC, platforms would struggle to meet the varying legal requirements, potentially limiting their ability to offer services in certain regions. 5. Protects the financial ecosystem Unverified accounts pose a risk not only to the platform but also to the broader financial ecosystem. By implementing KYC, global account providers contribute to a safer financial environment, reducing the likelihood of systemic risks caused by fraud or illicit activities. This protection benefits all stakeholders, from individual users to banks and governments. The KYC process: What to expect While KYC requirements vary slightly depending on the platform and jurisdiction, the process generally involves the following steps: Personal information submission : Users provide basic details, including their full name, date of birth, nationality, and contact information. Identity verification : This typically requires uploading a government-issued ID, such as a passport, driver’s licence, or national ID card. Proof of address : Users may need to submit a utility bill, bank statement, or other official document that confirms their residential address. Additional checks : Depending on the platform, users may need to provide further details, such as their source of funds, tax identification number, or a selfie holding their ID for facial recognition. Verification review : The platform reviews the submitted documents, often using automated systems or manual checks, to confirm the user’s identity. Approval or follow-up : Once verified, the user gains full access to the account. If there are discrepancies, the platform may request additional documents or clarification. The process can take anywhere from a few minutes to a few days, depending on the platform’s efficiency and the complexity of the user’s case. Challenges of KYC for global account users While KYC is essential, it can present challenges for users, particularly those new to global accounts or operating in regions with limited access to formal documentation. Common hurdles include: Document availability : In some countries, obtaining government-issued IDs or proof of address can be difficult, especially for individuals in rural areas or those without fixed addresses. Language barriers : Since global accounts are used by global users, it is common to encounter language struggles when uploading supporting documents, as they may not be in the platform's primary language(s). Verification delays: Users may experience verification delays when using certain financial services, which can be frustrating. Many platforms with high volumes of applications or manual review processes can experience verification delays, frustrating users who need immediate access to their global accounts for time-sensitive transactions. Privacy concerns : Some users hesitate to share personal information due to fears of data breaches or misuse, particularly in regions with a history of data security issues. Use the same name format as it appears on your ID. Avoid using nicknames or abbreviations. Provide a well-lit, uncluttered background for selfies. Submit documents in the recommended format (e.g., JPEG or PDF). Check your email regularly in case the provider requests additional information. Ensure all uploads are clear, no glares or blurs. It is in line with global best financial practices, ensuring financial systems are not exploited for financial crimes. Grey is committed to making global accounts accessible. title: John Storey and the Solar Spirit — A Life Devoted to Sustainability and Innovation
summary: In 1987, a newspaper ad caught the eye of a physics professor in Sydney. It was a call to adventure: build a car powered only by the sun and race it 3,000 kilometers across the Australian Outback. That professor was John Storey— and nearly four decades later, Storey is still at the heart of the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge.
body_text: In 1987, a newspaper ad caught the eye of a physics professor in Sydney. It was a call to adventure: build a car powered only by the sun and race it 3,000 kilometers across the Australian Outback. That professor was John Storey—and he’s been answering that call ever since. Nearly four decades later, Storey is still at the heart of the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge , now serving as its Chief Scientist. But his story is more than a tale of solar cars. It’s about a lifelong commitment to sustainability, a passion for mentoring young innovators, and a belief that technology can—and must—make the world better. From Garage to Global Stage Storey’s first solar car was built in a suburban garage with his wife and two brothers-in-law. “We were really all just having fun,” he said. Sponsored by Australian entrepreneur Dick Smith, the Team Marsupial solar car placed fourth in the inaugural race. “We just missed out on a podium finish, but we learned a great deal.” That experience sparked a career-long involvement. Storey now leads a global team of volunteer scientists and engineers who shape the rules, inspect the cars, and ensure the race remains fair, safe, and forward-looking. “While one event is taking place, we're already starting to revise the regulations for the next,” he said. A Teacher at Heart Storey’s greatest joy isn’t the cars—it’s the people. “The biggest product of the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge are the people,” he said. “These are largely student teams, and the training they get equips them to go out and make innovations in the corporate world.” Storey’s seen it firsthand. “The electric car charging company Tritium spun off from a Queensland University team. Some of the early participants went on to work at Tesla. And when we needed engineers for our Antarctic observatories, we turned to the Sunswift Solar Car team.” Living the Mission Storey doesn’t just talk sustainability—he lives it. After retiring from the University of New South Wales, he and his wife moved to a 600-acre off-grid property near Canberra. “We have 16 kilowatts of solar panels, 48 kilowatt-hours of batteries, and a small diesel generator we rarely use,” he said. The Storeys heat their home with wood from their land and drive a Hyundai Kona EV—his third electric car. “Once you've driven an electric car, you can never drive a gas car again. It just seems so silly.” But going off-grid isn’t without challenges. “Most EVs don’t have a spare tire or enough ground clearance. And almost none have AM radios, which are essential in rural Australia where there’s no internet or FM signal.” Still, Storey finds the lifestyle rewarding. “It’s fun, it’s challenging, and in some ways it’s more relaxing. We’re not dependent on the grid, and that gives us peace of mind.” A Legacy of Optimism Despite the environmental and political challenges facing the world, Storey remains hopeful for a sustainable future. “This event gives me hope,” he said. “It tells me that with enough will, we can make this world a much better place.” He sees the Solar Challenge as a beacon. “It makes it crystal clear that you don’t need to use a lot of energy to move people around. These cars weigh 250 kilos with the driver and can travel 100 kilometers an hour powered only by sunlight.” And while he doesn’t believe solar cars will become mainstream—“You still need a battery, and it’s more practical to charge it from a fixed panel”—he sees the race as a vital incubator for ideas. “The event doesn’t exist in isolation,” he said. “It’s embedded in universities, tech institutes, and industry. Innovation flows in both directions.” For Storey, the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge is more than a race. It’s a community, a classroom, and a cause. And after nearly 40 years, he’s still in love with it. “To be honest, the main reason I keep coming back is because it is just so much fun. It’s such an adventure. And the thing I like most of all are the people.” Dr. Storey in the 1987 Team Marsupial Solar Car Dr. Storey (center) and teammates working on their solar car in their garage-turned-workshop Team Marsupial car at the finish line near Adelaide Dr. Storey (front left) with 2023 officials This Mr. Green blog is part of our special coverage of the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge 2025 and Team αCentauri’s challenger class solar race car, #85 Silvretta. title: So, you’ve scheduled a consultation with a doula — what should you ask? A Parent’s Guide
body_text: Congratulations—you're thinking about hiring a doula! Whether for birth, postpartum, or both, this decision can transform your journey into one of empowerment, connection, and support. ‍ Why hiring a doula matters Partnering with a certified doula has been linked to: Lower Cesarean rates Fewer labor interventions (like Pitocin or forceps) Higher APGAR scores for newborns Better satisfaction with the birth experience Increased breastfeeding success and bonding Reduced risk of postpartum mood disorders Doulas don’t just support the birthing person—they uplift partners, grandparents, and extended family too. Think of them as your emotional anchor and informational guide through one of life’s biggest transitions. ‍ Step 1: Build your short-list Start by gathering names of doulas who might be a good fit. Search through Doula Directories Loula Doula Directory Find doulas who serve your county and accept your insurance DoulaMatch.Net DONA International Doula Directory Ask friends, family, or your OB/midwife for recommendations Connect with local parenting groups or birth educators Look for someone whose style , philosophy , and presence resonate with you and anyone else who are along the parenting journey with you. Oftentimes, many people speak to several doulas before finding their right match. ‍ Step 2: Set Up Consultations Many times, especially if you've never worked with a doula before, it's hard to envision the support a doula can provide. If you reach out to 5 different doulas, it's likely that you will hear 5 different approaches to doula care. It's okay if you don't have a list of criteria when you walk into these interviews. Come in to these consultations with an open mind to hearing the doula's approach to doula care! Meet in a relaxed, neutral setting like a café or on Zoom Have your partner join if possible—they’ll be supported too! Ask about availability and pricing upfront This is your chance to get a feel for the doula’s personality and approach—don’t be afraid to take notes or ask follow-ups. Don't be shy about letting the doula know that you're speaking with other doulas and that you will get back to them. You should never feel pressured to have an immediate answer after a consultation! ‍ Step 3: Questions to Ask When Interviewing a Doula Here are the key areas to explore: Philosophy & Approach What motivated you to become a doula? How do you describe your birth/postpartum support style? What comfort measures do you use (massage, rebozo, visualization, etc.)? Background & Experience What training have you completed? Which organization? Are you certified or pursuing certification (e.g., CD(DONA))? How many births or families have you supported? Services & Fees Have you worked with insurance? What existing doula packages can I expect? If you want to pay for your doula with insurance Do you provide any non-covered services for a fee? If you want to pay for your doula out-of-pocket What does your fee include—prenatal visits, labor support, postpartum care? How do you handle billing or sliding scale options (if any)? Logistics & Communication How will visits be structured before and after the birth? Do you offer virtual support? In what format? Can I text you? How responsive can I expect you to be ifi have questions? When do you go on call? How should we reach you when labor starts? Do you have a backup doula? Can we meet them? How long do you stay after the birth? Partner & Family Support How do you support partners during labor? Do you offer sibling support or guidance? What is your approach to newborn care and breastfeeding support? Health & Safety Are you CPR certified? Are your vaccinations (like Tdap or flu) current? Have you completed a background check? ‍ Step 4: Reflect & Decide After each interview, take a moment to reflect: Did you feel comfortable and listened to? Did the doula ask meaningful questions about your hopes and concerns? Did their answers align with your values and preferences? Sometimes, the right match is clear right away. Other times, it takes sleeping on it. Trust your gut—and act fast once you know. Doulas book up quickly! ‍ Step 5: Finalize & Hire Once you’ve chosen the right doula: Review and sign a contract outlining services, fees, and expectations If applciable, Pay any retainer or deposit as agreed Let the other doulas you interviewed know you’ve made a decision—it’s a kind and appreciated gesture Final Thoughts Choosing a doula is more than checking boxes—it’s about finding someone who gets you. Someone who will hold space for your fears and dreams, who’ll celebrate your strength, and who’ll stay by your side when things don’t go to plan. Take your time. Trust your intuition. And remember—this is your birth, your baby, your story. The right doula will honor that. ‍ ‍

title: Improvements to Campaign Billing and Sending Logic - Relate Changelog
summary: The billing criteria and sending rules for the Relate Campaign feature have been updated.
body_text: Overview The billing model and sending rules for the Campaign feature in Relate have been updated. 1/ Billing Model Changed to Subscriber-Based The billing structure for Relate’s email marketing feature, Campaign , is now based on the number of Subscribers . A Subscriber refers to a contact that has received at least one email and is calculated as follows: Subscribers = Contacts who received at least one email − (Unsubscribers + Bounced) Unsubscriber : A contact who clicked the unsubscribe link in an email sent from the Workspace. Bounced : A contact whose email could not be delivered due to an invalid address. Unlike traditional email marketing services that charge based on the total number of registered contacts—including those with no engagement—this subscriber-based model ensures billing reflects actual usage. The Campaign feature is available free of charge for up to 1,000 subscribers. 2/ Timing for Finalizing Campaign Recipients Updated In email campaigns, recipient lists are selected to designate who receives the emails. The timing of when campaign recipients are finalized has been changed: Before : Determined at the time of email sending Now : Determined at the time of email scheduling As a result, contacts added to a list after the campaign has been scheduled will not be included in the campaign. For example, if a campaign is scheduled at 3:00 PM for delivery at 3:10 PM to List A, any contacts added to List A at 3:05 PM will not receive the campaign. 3/ Automatic Suspension of Campaigns with High Bounce Rates A Bounce occurs when an email cannot be delivered due to an invalid address. If the bounce rate exceeds the thresholds below, the campaign will be automatically stopped , and the status will change to stopped . Fewer than 1,000 total sends : Stopped if there are 50 or more bounces 1,000 or more total sends : Stopped if bounce rate exceeds 5% The reason for suspension will be displayed as a red warning message in the campaign’s Analytics view. 4/ Canceled Email Handling Emails are automatically blocked from being sent to addresses that may harm the domain's sender reputation. In such cases, the Status of the contact is marked as Canceled . Common reasons include: Attempting to send to a contact with a history of unsubscribing Attempting to send to a contact with a history of bounces Attempting to send to a high-risk domain (e.g., non-existent or unresponsive) Delivery failure due to system errors Hovering over the Canceled status in Campaign > Analytics > Status provides additional information on the cancellation reason.

body_text: Complete Guide to Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) 2025: How to Win in AI Search The AI Search Revolution is Here - And It's Massive The numbers tell a compelling story of how rapidly search behavior is shifting toward AI-powered platforms: ChatGPT has exploded to over 400 million weekly users - making it the 10th most visited website globally and prompting users to set it as their default search engine [1]. This represents the fastest adoption of any technology platform in history. Perplexity AI processes 780 million queries monthly with 129 million visits, growing at over 20% month-over-month [2]. More remarkably, the average query length on Perplexity is 10-11 words compared to Google's 2-3 keywords, indicating users prefer conversational, detailed queries when interacting with AI. Google AI Overviews now appear in over 13% of all U.S. desktop searches and reach more than 1 billion users across 100+ countries [3]. When AI Overviews are present, they often satisfy user intent without requiring clicks to external websites. Perhaps most striking: 70% of consumers already trust generative AI search results , and 79% are expected to use AI-enhanced search within the next year [4]. According to Andreessen Horowitz, 60% of U.S. consumers used an AI chatbot to research or decide on a product in the last 30 days. Leading this AI search revolution are companies like Geostar , who have pioneered Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) strategies that help businesses establish authority in AI-powered discovery channels. As AI adoption accelerates, the opportunity to become the trusted source that AI systems reference becomes increasingly critical. What is Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)? Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the strategic practice of optimizing digital content to improve visibility and citation rates in AI-powered search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and other large language models. Unlike traditional SEO that focuses on ranking web pages in search results, GEO ensures your brand appears within the AI-generated responses themselves. When someone asks ChatGPT "What's the best project management software for small teams?" you want your product mentioned in the answer, not just hope they'll click through to your website. GEO focuses on being the source of truth that AI systems reference, cite, and trust. How GEO Differs from Traditional SEO While GEO builds upon SEO fundamentals, it requires new approaches for the AI era: Traditional SEO Approach Goal: Rank pages for specific keywords Success Metric: Click-through rates from search results Content Strategy: Keyword-focused pages optimized for search crawlers Authority Building: Backlinks and domain authority GEO Approach Goal: Get cited and referenced in AI responses Success Metric: Citation frequency across AI platforms Content Strategy: Answer-first content optimized for AI comprehension Authority Building: Entity recognition and cross-platform mentions Key Insight: Research from Princeton University demonstrates that GEO optimization can boost content visibility by up to 40% across diverse AI search queries, while traditional keyword-stuffing techniques prove ineffective for large language models [5]. The 7 Essential GEO Strategies for 2025 1. Master Answer-First Content Architecture AI systems prioritize content that directly answers user questions with clear, comprehensive responses. Structure your content to lead with definitive answers, then provide supporting detail. Implementation: Open each section with a 40-60 word answer block that directly addresses the query Use question-based H2 headings like "How Do You Choose the Right CRM?" Include FAQ schema markup to help AI systems identify question-answer pairs Create scannable bullet lists and numbered steps for complex processes Example Structure: ## How Do You Implement Generative Engine Optimization? Generative Engine Optimization requires a systematic approach focusing on content clarity, entity authority, and AI comprehension. Start by conducting AI citation audits, then optimize content structure for answer extraction, and finally build cross-platform authority through strategic mentions and quality backlinks. ### Step 1: Conduct AI Citation Audits [Detailed explanation] ### Step 2: Optimize Content Architecture [Detailed explanation] 2. Build Authoritative Entity Recognition AI systems heavily weight content from recognized authorities within specific domains. Establish your brand as a trusted entity through consistent messaging and expert positioning. Authority Building Tactics: Maintain identical company descriptions across all platforms (website, LinkedIn, directories) Include founder/team credentials and years of experience prominently Cite authoritative sources and include expert quotes in your content Publish original research and data that others can reference Participate in industry podcasts, interviews, and expert roundups Quote Integration Example: "According to Stanford AI researcher Dr. Sarah Chen, 'Companies that optimize for AI citation see 3x higher brand recall in assisted search scenarios.' This finding aligns with our internal data showing 127% improvement in citation rates for optimized content." 3. Optimize for Conversational Query Patterns AI search users employ longer, more conversational queries. Optimize for how people actually ask questions, not just what they type into Google. Conversational Optimization: Target 10-15 word question phrases like "What's the best way to track AI citations for my business?" Address follow-up questions within the same content piece Use natural language and avoid keyword stuffing Include related questions users might ask in the same session Research Insight: 50% of Perplexity queries result in follow-up questions, indicating users prefer exploratory, conversational search sessions rather than single-query interactions. 4. Implement Comprehensive Schema Markup Structured data helps AI systems understand your content context and extract relevant information for citations. Priority Schema Types: Organization Schema: Establish your company as a recognized entity FAQ Schema: Mark up question-answer pairs for easy AI extraction Article Schema: Include author credentials and publication dates HowTo Schema: Structure step-by-step guides for AI comprehension Product Schema: Detail product features and specifications 5. Create Citation-Worthy Statistics and Data AI systems frequently cite specific statistics and research findings. Include original data points that others will want to reference. Data Integration Strategy: Conduct original surveys and publish findings Track industry benchmarks and share year-over-year comparisons Include specific percentages and timeframes: "94% of enterprise users report ROI within 6 months" Cite methodology and sample sizes for credibility Create downloadable reports that establish thought leadership Example: "According to Geostar's 2025 AI Visibility Index, companies implementing GEO strategies see 156% higher citation rates compared to those relying solely on traditional SEO techniques." 6. Leverage Multi-Platform Content Distribution AI systems draw from diverse content sources. Distribute your insights across platforms where AI training data is sourced. Distribution Channels: Reddit: Participate in relevant subreddits with helpful, non-promotional advice Quora: Answer questions in your expertise area with detailed responses LinkedIn Articles: Publish thought leadership content Industry Forums: Contribute to Stack Overflow, specialized communities Podcast Transcripts: Ensure spoken content is transcribed and indexed Strategic Approach: Don't just broadcast - engage authentically in communities where your expertise adds value. AI systems recognize genuine contributions over promotional content. 7. Monitor and Optimize AI Citation Performance Track how often your content appears in AI responses and optimize based on performance data. Monitoring Strategy: Manually test target queries across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews Use emerging tools like Semrush AI Toolkit to track citation frequency Monitor branded searches for AI-driven traffic increases Track referral traffic from AI platforms (when available) Document which content formats get cited most frequently Advanced GEO Techniques for Competitive Advantage Entity Disambiguation and Knowledge Graph Optimization Help AI systems clearly identify your brand and associate it with relevant topics: Create detailed "About" pages with clear entity descriptions Maintain consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) across all platforms Link to authoritative sources that mention your brand Use schema markup to define relationships between entities Answer Box Optimization Since AI often pulls from featured snippets and answer boxes: Format content for snippet capture with clear, concise answers Use table format for comparison data Include numbered lists for step-by-step processes Optimize page speed and mobile experience Cross-Reference Authority Building Create a network of content that reinforces your expertise: Reference your other relevant content with strategic internal linking Guest post on authoritative sites in your industry Participate in expert roundups and industry surveys Build relationships with journalists who cover your space Common GEO Mistakes to Avoid 1. Over-Optimizing for Keywords AI systems detect and penalize keyword stuffing. Focus on natural language and comprehensive answers rather than keyword density. 2. Ignoring Mobile and Voice Search Many AI interactions happen on mobile devices. Ensure content is mobile-friendly and optimized for voice queries. 3. Neglecting Technical SEO AI systems still need to crawl and index your content. Maintain strong technical SEO fundamentals including fast loading speeds, clean code, and proper indexing. 4. Creating Thin or Duplicate Content AI systems favor comprehensive, unique content. Avoid creating multiple pages with similar information or thin content that doesn't add value. 5. Forgetting Local SEO For local businesses, maintain accurate Google My Business listings and local directory presence, as AI systems often reference local search data. Measuring GEO Success: New Metrics for the AI Age Traditional SEO metrics remain important, but GEO requires additional measurement approaches: Primary GEO Metrics AI Citation Rate: Frequency of mentions across AI platforms Answer Box Appearances: How often content appears in featured snippets Entity Recognition Accuracy: How correctly AI systems identify your brand Conversational Query Rankings: Performance for long-tail, question-based queries Secondary Metrics Direct Traffic Increases: Users discovering you through AI and searching directly Brand Mention Volume: Increased discussions across platforms Expert Quote Requests: Journalists and content creators seeking your input Partnership Opportunities: Collaboration requests based on thought leadership The Future of Search: GEO as Competitive Advantage Gartner predicts that by 2026, traditional search volume will drop by 25%, with organic search traffic potentially decreasing by over 50% as consumers embrace AI-powered search alternatives [6]. This isn't a distant future - it's happening now. Companies that invest in GEO today will establish competitive moats that become increasingly difficult to replicate. While competitors struggle to adapt their traditional SEO strategies, GEO-optimized brands will dominate AI-driven discovery. The Integration Approach The most successful organizations treat GEO as an evolution of SEO, not a replacement: Maintain strong technical SEO as the foundation for content discovery Layer on GEO optimizations for AI comprehension and citation Create content that serves both human readers and AI systems Build authority through traditional and AI-focused channels Getting Started with GEO: Your 30-Day Action Plan Week 1: Audit and Assess Test your brand across major AI platforms (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI) Document current AI citation frequency Identify gaps in entity recognition and brand representation Analyze competitor presence in AI responses Week 2: Content Optimization Rewrite key landing pages with answer-first architecture Add FAQ schema to product and service pages Create comprehensive resource guides for your expertise areas Optimize meta descriptions for conversational queries Week 3: Authority Building Pitch expert commentary to industry publications Create original research or surveys in your space Update all business listings with consistent information Begin participating in relevant online communities Week 4: Monitor and Refine Set up tracking for AI citations and mentions Test optimized content across AI platforms Gather feedback on answer quality and completeness Plan next month's content based on AI response analysis Conclusion: The AI Search Advantage The shift from traditional search to AI-powered discovery represents the most significant change in information access since Google's PageRank algorithm revolutionized the web. Just as early Google adopters gained massive advantages over competitors stuck in directory-based thinking, businesses that master GEO now will dominate the AI search landscape. Generative Engine Optimization isn't just about visibility - it's about becoming the trusted source that AI systems turn to when users need answers in your domain. While your competitors wonder why their traffic is declining, you'll be building relationships with millions of users through AI-powered discovery. The future of search is generative, conversational, and AI-driven. The question isn't whether you should optimize for this new reality - it's whether you'll lead the transition or scramble to catch up. Ready to establish your AI search dominance? title: Migrate your MongoDB Data API in 30 minutes
summary: MongoDB is deprecating its Atlas Data API. With Modelence, you can provision a fully functional, production-ready replacement in about 30 minutes - no heavy backend work required.
body_text: Introduction MongoDB has recently announced the deprecation of its Atlas Data API (as well as Custom HTTPS Endpoints) for Atlas App Services - set to become unavailable after September 30, 2025. This affects many developers and applications that rely on HTTP-based CRUD access to Atlas clusters. Official MongoDB deprecation notice What is MongoDB Data API? The Data API provided a simple, RESTful HTTP interface directly to your MongoDB Atlas cluster - developers could perform CRUD operations via HTTP requests without needing a full backend or client driver. It was especially useful for serverless workflows, quick integrations, and frontend-only applications. Who used it - and what's happening now? Many serverless apps, low-code tools, and rapid prototyping platforms relied heavily on the Data API. These users are now facing pending disruptions as MongoDB phases it out. On September 30, 2025, both the Data API and Custom HTTPS Endpoints are planned to be removed. MongoDB has published documentation to help users migrate, recommending alternatives like Express + Drivers, Cloud Functions, and partner solutions. But for most teams, adopting these options means a complex setup process, significant time investment, and, in many cases, the added challenge of migrating data. Introducing Modelence: Your drop-in replacement Replacing the deprecated Data API is easy. With Modelence, you can provision a fully functional, production-ready MongoDB Data API replacement in about 30 minutes - no heavy backend work required. Step-by-step migration with Modelence Create a new Modelence app and cloud environment by following the setup wizard. Register at cloud.modelence.com . Choose the data-api template from example apps. Copy the generated command and run it in your terminal to deploy data-api to your Modelence Cloud. In the Modelence Dashboard, view your app deployment status in the Deployments tab. Once it's deployed (which will take 5-10 minutes), navigate to Application → Custom Configuration section and set your Data API key and MongoDB URI. You can always change them, and we recommend rotating API keys periodically for security purposes. Your endpoint will have the following format: http://<your-app>.prod.modelence.app Now you can use the following endpoints to invoke your Data API: Login example: Use the API key configured in the previous step. curl --location 'http://<your-app>.prod.modelence.app/auth/providers/api-key/login' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "key": "123" }' This will return an access token, which should be used in all API calls as an authorization bearer. Insert document example: curl --location 'http://<your-app>.prod.modelence.app/data/v1/action/insertOne' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <access-token>' \ --data '{ "dataSource": "Cluster0", "database": "dataApi", "collection": "users", "document": { "name": "John Sample", "age": 42 } }' For an interactive feel, use the Postman-like interface available at http://<your-app>.prod.modelence.app .

title: Xiao-I Corporation Celebrates Eight Consecutive Years Empowering Premium Kitchen Appliance Leader with AI-Driven Customer Experience
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Xiao-I Corporation (NASDAQ: AIXI), a global leader in artificial intelligence solutions, today announced the renewal of its strategic...
body_text: SHANGHAI , Aug. 11, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Xiao-I Corporation (NASDAQ: AIXI ), a global leader in artificial intelligence solutions, today announced the renewal of its strategic partnership for the eighth consecutive year with a leading Chinese manufacturer and marketer of high-end kitchen appliances. This long-term collaboration underscores the critical role of Xiao-I's AI solutions in transforming customer service, sales, and after-sales support for the consumer goods industry. Leveraging Xiao-I's flagship Dialogue Robot (iBot) and IKBase (Intelligent Knowledge Base) solutions, the partnership has created a seamlessly integrated intelligent service ecosystem supporting thousands of customer service agents, e-commerce representatives, and field technicians. Key AI-Powered Services and Value Delivered: Unified Omnichannel Customer Support: Providing 24/7 intelligent customer service across phone, web, app, and social channels (via iBot) for product inquiries, troubleshooting, and post-purchase support, significantly improving first-contact resolution rates and customer satisfaction. E-commerce Sales Enablement: Powering intelligent chatbots on e-commerce platforms and brand websites to assist online shoppers with product selection, specifications, promotions, and order tracking, driving conversion rates and enhancing the digital shopping journey. Scalable Technical Support & Dispatch: Equipping the client's vast network of over ten thousand field service technicians with AI assistance (via iBot & IKBase). Technicians access instant troubleshooting guides, installation manuals, and parts information, enabling faster, more accurate in-home service and efficient appointment management. Operational Efficiency & Cost Savings: Automating high volumes of routine inquiries and tasks across service, sales, and technical support, freeing human staff to handle complex issues and strategic initiatives, leading to demonstrable cost reductions and productivity gains. "Eight years of continuous partnership with this industry leader is a powerful testament to the tangible impact of our cognitive AI solutions beyond traditional sectors," said spokesperson of Xiao-I Corporation. "For premium consumer brands, delivering exceptional, consistent, and efficient service – from the first online inquiry to the technician's visit – is paramount. Our integrated iBot and IKBase platform provides the intelligence backbone to unify customer engagement, empower staff, and optimize complex operational chains involving thousands of agents and technicians, ultimately driving superior brand loyalty." About Xiao-I Corporation Xiao-I Corporation is a leading cognitive intelligence enterprise in China that offers a diverse range of business solutions and services in artificial intelligence, covering natural language processing, voice and image recognition, machine learning, and affective computing. Since its inception in 2001, the Company has developed an extensive portfolio of cognitive intelligence technologies that are highly suitable and have been applied to a wide variety of business cases. Xiao-I powers its cognitive intelligence products and services with its cutting-edge, proprietary AI technologies to enable and promote industrial digitization, intelligent upgrading, and transformation. For more information, please visit: www.xiaoi.com .
